c74object.name: ossia.v8connector
c74object.digest: Declare ossia parameters from a script
c74object.description: Create a node of the ossia namespace, like ossia.model, whose parameters are declared by messages instead of ossia.parameter objects. A v8 or v8ui script adds, removes and sets the parameters, and receives the values changed by any other source on the left outlet. The node registers under the ossia.model, ossia.device or ossia.client found in the patcher hierarchy, or under the global device.

inlet.name: Message input
inlet.description: add, remove, clear, set, bind, unbind, address, namespace and get messages

outlet.name: Values
outlet.description: A message per changed parameter, the relative address followed by the value, bounded to the parameter's range then filtered by the parameter (disabled, muted, repetition when @repetitions is 0), as at the outlet of every ossia object. A value set through this instance comes back here only when the bounded value differs from the one sent. The default of a leaf comes out here once the leaf exists, a bound address outputs the value it finds when it reaches the parameter, and ready is sent once the object has registered, so that a script can replay its declarations. Every refusal of add, bind, set, remove or unbind also comes out here as refused followed by the address and the reason, through the same deferred queue as the values. ready and refused are reserved addresses.

outlet.name: Info outlet
outlet.description: address, add, remove, clear, bind, unbind and error messages; namespace_size then one line per parameter after namespace; the attribute name and its value after get

objarg.name: Name
objarg.digest: Name of the node in the ossia namespace
objarg.description: With a name, the declared parameters are created under a node of that name, which is created by the first add and stays, even without parameters, until the object is deleted, like an ossia.model. An instance that only binds creates no node, like an ossia.remote. When several nodes have the same name, instances (name.1, name.2, etc...) are created, as for ossia.model. Without a name, the parameters are created directly under the node of the enclosing ossia.model, or the root of the enclosing ossia.device or ossia.client, or the root of the global device, next to the ossia.parameter objects: an address already taken, by another instance or by an ossia.parameter, is refused (refused <address> already exists) and never renamed, and the instance removes only its own parameters. bind addresses are relative to the enclosing model or device in both cases.

method.name: add
method.digest: Create a parameter under the node
method.description: The message add followed by a relative address and attributes creates a parameter, with the same attribute names as ossia.parameter: @type, @min, @max, @range, @unit, @default, @clip, @mode, @description, @tags, @priority, @rate, @critical, @invisible, @mute, @repetitions, @enable, @recall_safe. @type is required. A numeric type (float, int, vec2f, vec3f, vec4f) requires @min and @max, or @range: the declaration is refused otherwise. A unit imposes the type of its values (color.rgb is vec3f, color.rgba vec4f, gain.db float): a declared @type that the unit would change is refused, with the reason. @clip accepts none, the OSCQuery name of the free mode, as well as free, both, low, high, wrap and fold. A refusal is reported on the right outlet and as refused <address> <reason> on the left outlet. Declaring the same leaf again with the same attributes is accepted and does nothing.

method.name: remove
method.description: The message remove followed by a relative address removes the parameter declared by this instance at that address.

method.name: clear
method.digest: Remove every parameter of this instance
method.description: The message clear removes every parameter declared by this instance. The node itself stays.

method.name: set
method.digest: Set the value of a parameter
method.description: The message set followed by an address (a declared leaf, or a bound address) and a value pushes the value to the parameter, which stores it as sent, like ossia.parameter. The value is sent to the network and to every other ossia object that listens to this address; each object bounds it to the range at its outlet. It does not come back on the left outlet of this instance, unless the bounded value differs from the one sent (clip, type conversion): the bounded value then comes back, as if it came from another source.

method.name: bind
method.digest: Follow a parameter that exists elsewhere
method.description: The message bind followed by an address subscribes to a parameter declared by another object, an ossia.parameter or another ossia.v8connector, without creating anything. The address follows the rules of ossia.remote: relative to the enclosing model or device, absolute with a leading slash, or device:/address; patterns are accepted. The type and the range stay those of the owner. Values changed by another source leave the left outlet under the bound address, set pushes to the owner's parameter, and the subscription follows the parameter when it disappears and comes back. The right outlet sends bind followed by the address and the number of parameters currently followed.

method.name: unbind
method.description: The message unbind followed by a bound address drops the subscription. The parameter itself is untouched.

method.name: address
method.description: The message address followed by a symbol sets the name of the node and registers it again with its parameters.

method.name: get
method.digest: Output the value of a node attribute
method.description: The message get followed by global_address, description, tags, invisible, priority, recall_safe or zombie outputs that attribute of the instance's node on the right outlet. An instance without a name, or that only binds, has no node of its own: nothing comes out.

method.name: namespace
method.digest: Output list of all parameters and their current values
method.description: The namespace message outputs on the right outlet namespace_size followed by the number of entries, then one namespace message per parameter registered under this node, with its address and current value. An instance without a name, or that only binds, outputs namespace_size 0.

attribute.name: bundle
attribute.digest: Send the values of a tick together, in OSC bundles
attribute.description: The bundle attribute (default: 1) groups the values this instance sets during a tick: they leave together at the end of the tick, in OSC bundles, through the protocol of each parameter (a client's OSCQuery mirror splits them under 1400 bytes over UDP, the server of a device gets bundles of at most 1400 bytes). A parameter set several times in a tick leaves once, with its last value; with @repetitions 0, a value equal to the current one does not leave. 0 sends one message per value.

attribute.name: description
attribute.description: The description attribute (default: none) sets the description of the node. Without a name, the instance has no node of its own and the attribute does nothing.

attribute.name: invisible
attribute.description: The invisible attribute (default: 0) hides the node from remote clients. Without a name, the attribute does nothing.

attribute.name: priority
attribute.description: The priority attribute (default: 0) is stored on the node, as ossia.model does. It does not order the outputs of ossia.v8connector: ossia-max orders the outputs of ossia.parameter and ossia.remote only. The default of a leaf comes out of the left outlet once the leaf exists, and a bound address outputs the value it finds as soon as it reaches the parameter, in declaration order.

attribute.name: recall_safe
attribute.digest: Enable or disable value update when recalling preset
attribute.description: The recall_safe attribute (default: off) allows to prevent value update when recalling a preset. Without a name, the attribute does nothing.

attribute.name: tags
attribute.description: The tags attribute (default: none) associates a variable number of tags with this node. Without a name, the attribute does nothing.
